_readme: Built-in game content for Twelve. Edit this file, then run: node supabase/content/build.mjs (it rewrites supabase/twelve_content.sql). In quiz questions the FIRST choice is the right one; the build script shuffles the choices. For Two Truths and a Tradition, the first choice is the made-up one. For Speed-Matching, pairs are written left → right and the script shuffles the right-hand column.

trivia.title: Holiday Trivia
trivia.intro: Ten questions about the season. No googling — Santa is watching.
questions: What are the names of Santa's reindeer that start with D?
Which country started the tradition of the Christmas tree?
In 'A Christmas Carol', what is Scrooge's first name?
How many gifts in total are given in 'The Twelve Days of Christmas'?
Which plant is known as the 'Christmas flower' and comes from Mexico?
In the movie 'Elf', what are the four main food groups of elves?
Candy, candy canes, candy corn, syrup
What is the best-selling single of all time, according to Guinness?
All I Want for Christmas Is You
Which beverage company's ads helped popularize the modern red-suited Santa?
What do people traditionally put on top of a Christmas tree?

two_truths.title: Two Truths and a Tradition
two_truths.intro: Each set has two real holiday traditions from around the world and one we made up. Spot the fake.
questions: In Finland, families hide a frozen herring in the garden for children to find on Christmas morning.
In Norway, people hide their brooms on Christmas Eve so witches can't steal them.
In Japan, a bucket of KFC is a popular Christmas dinner.
In Portugal, children leave out a single sock filled with salt for the Three Kings' horses.
In Iceland, 13 mischievous 'Yule Lads' visit children in the nights before Christmas.
In Caracas, Venezuela, people roller-skate to early-morning Christmas Mass.
In Scotland, the first person to see snow on Christmas Eve must sing a carol on the doorstep.
In Ukraine, people decorate trees with artificial spider webs for good luck.
In Catalonia, a smiling log called Caga Tió is 'fed' and then hit with sticks until it gives out sweets.
In Denmark, the family that unwraps the most gifts must wash all the dishes on Boxing Day.
In Sweden, millions watch the same Donald Duck cartoon special every Christmas Eve at 3 PM.
In the Czech Republic, single women toss a shoe over their shoulder to predict whether they'll marry.
In Canada, people bury a candy cane in the snow and dig it up on New Year's Day for luck.
In Austria, a horned beast called Krampus roams the streets to scare naughty children.
In some American families, a pickle-shaped ornament is hidden in the tree and whoever finds it first gets a prize.
In Greece, people place a lemon under their pillow on Christmas Eve to dream of the year ahead.
In Guatemala, people sweep their homes and burn a pile of rubbish in 'La Quema del Diablo'.
In the Philippines, the city of San Fernando holds a Giant Lantern Festival.

two_truths.title: Two Truths and a Tradition: Round Two
two_truths.intro: Another lap around the world. Two of these are real. One is pure fiction.
questions: In Belgium, children polish a spoon and leave it on the windowsill for Saint Nicholas to fill with honey.
In Italy, a kindly witch named La Befana delivers gifts on January 5th.
In Poland, an extra place is set at the Christmas Eve table for an unexpected guest.
In Ireland, people race wheelbarrows full of holly through town on Christmas Eve.
In Ireland, a tall candle is placed in the window on Christmas Eve to welcome travelers.
In Mexico, Las Posadas re-enacts Mary and Joseph's search for shelter over nine nights.
In Switzerland, people tie bells to their pets' collars so Santa won't trip over them.
In Australia, Christmas lunch is often a barbecue or seafood at the beach.
In the Netherlands, Sinterklaas arrives by steamboat in mid-November.
In England, the youngest family member must wear a paper crown upside down until dessert.
In England, families pull Christmas crackers that pop and hold paper crowns and jokes.
In Wales, a horse skull on a pole called the Mari Lwyd goes door to door with singers.
In Estonia, families leave a lit candle in the freezer to keep winter spirits happy.
In Estonia, families visit the sauna together on Christmas Eve.
In Ethiopia, many people celebrate Christmas (Genna) on January 7th.
In France, children leave carrots in their shoes for Santa's reindeer to find in April.
In France, a feast called Le Réveillon is held late on Christmas Eve.
In Provence, France, families serve thirteen desserts at Christmas.

bingo.title: Holiday Bingo
bingo.intro: Tap a square when it happens to you today. You have until the game closes, so come back and mark more. 3 points a square, 8 points a line.
squares: Someone sings a carol out loud
You hear 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'
You see a house with blinking lights
You spot an inflatable lawn decoration
You watch part of a holiday movie
You say 'Happy Holidays' to a stranger
You see a wreath on a door
You find a stray bit of glitter
You check a gift off your list
You see someone carrying a big shopping bag

bingo.title: Holiday Bingo: Round Two
bingo.intro: A fresh card for a fresh day. Same rules: mark squares as they happen until the game closes.
squares: Someone asks what you want for Christmas
You hear a holiday ad on TV or radio
You find a gift you forgot you bought
You untangle a string of lights
You see an elf (decoration or costume)

scavenger.title: Holiday Scavenger Hunt
scavenger.intro: The clock starts when you press Start. Find each item and snap a photo. Faster means more points: full speed bonus inside 10 minutes.
items: Something red and something green together
A mug you'd drink cocoa from

scavenger.title: Scavenger Hunt: Round Two
scavenger.intro: New list, same clock. Find, snap, go! Full speed bonus inside 10 minutes.
items: A roll of wrapping paper or a gift bag
Something with a snowflake on it

photo.title: Photo Challenge
photo.intro: Take your best shot. The host picks the winner after the day closes.
photo.prompt: Recreate your favorite holiday movie scene with whatever's lying around the house.
photo.tips: Props are encouraged. Pets in costume are very encouraged.

photo.title: Photo Challenge: Round Two
photo.intro: One photo, one winner, chosen by the host once the day closes.
photo.prompt: Show us the most festive corner of your home.
photo.tips: Lights on, lamps off. Good angles win hearts.
